sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is inside the Henderson County Courthouse, 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville. It records documents Monday through Friday from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The main phone is 828-697-4901.

Staff run a recording counter. They check that a document meets the North Carolina Real Estate Recording Standards, but they cannot give legal advice, so ask your closing attorney what a deed should say. You can pay by check, cash, money order or card. Card payments carry a vendor fee that goes to the vendor.

The Tax Department's Land Records section works from the same courthouse. It builds the county's official index of tax listings from recorded deeds and Clerk of Court files, so a deed that reaches the register soon appears in the parcel data used for billing.

Land transactions in the county are archived here. The office lists these holdings:

  • Land transfers, easements, rights of way and surveys
  • Deeds of trust, mortgages and UCC filings
  • Separation agreements
  • Assumed business name (DBA) filings
  • Notary public oaths
  • Vital records, with certified copies at $10.00 and photocopies at $.25
  • Military records, recorded and certified for the veteran at no charge

Marriage licenses are by appointment only, between 10:00 AM and 3:00 PM on weekdays. Call instead of emailing. Assumed business name forms must be printed on one side of the paper only. Front-and-back printing fails the recording requirements and adds a non-standard document fee to the recording fees.

The online deed index runs from 1979 to the present and is hosted by a records vendor. You accept a disclaimer first. The site works best on a desktop or laptop with Chrome or Edge, cookies on and pop-up blocking off for the site.

To pull a plat, open the Register of Deeds system and choose View Images. Pick Plat as the book type, enter the recording year or Cabinet A, B or C as the book, and give the plat number as the page. Leading zeros are not needed. The county's guide lists slide ranges by year, such as 2024 at slides 15330 to 16020 and 2025 at slides 16021 to 16768, with 2026 starting at slide 16769. Older plats from 1988 forward follow the same numbering, and three early cabinets hold the oldest slides.

The online images carry no guarantee of accuracy. The official records stay in the courthouse office, so confirm anything important at the counter.

A privacy notice on the search page cites G.S. 132-1.8(g). Leave Social Security, driver license, bank account and card numbers off any document you file unless the law requires them. You can ask the register in writing to remove such a number from an online image, and there is no fee for that request.

State law sets the amounts, so Henderson County follows G.S. 161-10. Ask the office about any local charge for services outside recording.

Recording fees that apply in Henderson County
DocumentFee
General instrument$26.00 for 15 pages, plus $4.00 per added page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for 35 pages, plus $4.00 per added page
Satisfaction or cancellationNo fee

sections.h2: Deed stamp tax when you sell
sections.html:
The seller pays it, as the transferor named in the statute. The rate is $1.00 for each $500.00 of price or fraction of it, and the register collects it first.

Look for the line on your settlement statement before closing day. The rule is in G.S. 105-228.30.

sections.h2: What the 2027 reappraisal means for a seller
sections.html:
Values reset on January 1, 2027. Henderson reappraises real property every four years, well ahead of the eight-year minimum in G.S. 105-286, and the last reappraisal took effect in 2023.

Values follow market prices from recent qualified sales, and a mass appraisal groups similar properties together. It weighs location, construction type, age, replacement cost and zoning. A building still under construction on January 1 is valued by its percentage of completion. Land enrolled in the Present-Use Value Program for agriculture, horticulture or forestry can carry an assessed value below market.

The Tax Department counts about 71,500 parcels, and property taxes are an estimated 50 percent of the county operating budget in fiscal year 2027. The Board of Commissioners sets the rate and the Assessor sets values. The Tax Department has divisions for real property, personal property, exemptions and deferment, land records and collections. Programs cover elderly or disabled owners, disabled veteran owners, nonprofits, commercial farms and wildlife management. See the county reappraisal page.

The county had 122,375 people in July 2025, 5.2 percent above the April 2020 base. It has 61,173 housing units, and builders pulled 1,093 permits during 2025.

Owners occupy 75.0 percent of homes, valued at a median $351,400. Monthly owner costs are $1,608 with a mortgage and $482 without. Gross rent is near $1,187, and household income is $68,187. Adults past 65 are 29.1 percent of residents, so the property tax exclusions for older and disabled owners are worth a question to the Tax Department.

A short checklist keeps the document from being flagged or delayed at the counter.

  • Print on one side of letter or legal paper in black ink, using at least 10 point type.
  • State the instrument type across the head of page one and leave a three inch blank margin there.
  • Redact Social Security and account numbers unless the law requires them.
  • Put the drafter's name and the parcel number on page one.
  • Have your attorney file the satisfaction of any paid-off deed of trust.

If the deed fails the formatting standards, the register records it anyway after collecting an added nonstandard document fee. Staff can also issue a certified copy of anything the office recorded.

Bring the signed original, the parcel number, and a card or check for the fees. If you are not sure the formatting passes, call 828-697-4901 before you travel to the courthouse, since the counter closes at 5:00 PM and a document that needs fixing could miss the day.

A typical sale runs in this order. The attorney drafts the deed, you sign, the closing attorney delivers it to the counter, and the seller's stamp tax is collected before recording. Any paid-off deed of trust gets a satisfaction, which is free to record. Once recorded, the deed shows up in the county's land records and then in the parcel data the Tax Department uses for billing.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to record a deed?
faqs.a: Appointments are listed only for marriage licenses, which run 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM and are booked by phone. Recording is open during the regular weekday hours, and the office answers questions at 828-697-4901.

faqs.q: How far back does the online deed index go?
faqs.a: It covers 1979 to the present. For older plats, choose Plat as the book type and enter a year or Cabinet A, B or C. The county's plat guide gives the slide ranges.

faqs.q: Does Henderson County reappraise every year?
faqs.a: No. Real property is reappraised every four years, last in 2023, with the next effective January 1, 2027. State law requires one at least every eight years.

faqs.q: Can I pay by card at the Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Cards are accepted along with checks, cash and money orders. The vendor that processes the card adds a fee, and the county does not charge it.

faqs.q: What does a certified vital record cost?
faqs.a: A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage certificate is $10.00 with proper ID and an acceptable relationship to the person named. Photocopies are $.25.
